articles.title: Teslemetry gives Tesla commands a local Bluetooth route
articles.dek: Optional pairing lets Home Assistant control a nearby car even when its mobile connection or the cloud is unreachable.
body: Tesla owners using Teslemetry gain a local route for commands from Home Assistant. Optional Bluetooth pairing sends commands directly to a nearby car, keeping control possible when the car’s mobile connection or the cloud is unreachable.

Brett Adams adds automatic fallback to the cloud for individual commands when Bluetooth cannot handle them. Existing controls stay in their familiar places in Home Assistant, so the new connection works through the vehicle entities people already use.
A companion correction closes the Bluetooth link if an unexpected error interrupts pairing. A failed authorization attempt therefore does not leave the connection open.

pullRequests.title: Add Bluetooth control for Teslemetry vehicles
Disconnect Bluetooth link on unexpected pairing-task exception in Teslemetry

articles.title: ESPHome turns ESP32 boards into USB serial adapters
articles.dek: A new bridge connects a computer to serial equipment for debugging, programming and reading data.
body: Makers gain a way to use an ESPHome board as the USB connection to another device’s serial port. A new bridge supports ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-P4 boards, carrying data in both directions for console access, sensor logging or programming a device with a serial bootloader.

Keith Burzinski’s component follows the computer’s chosen connection speed and data format, and can carry reset and bootloader signals through optional pins. Multiple bridges can serve separate ports on one board.

The implementation was tested on an ESP32-S3 development board with a CH340 serial adapter, including a two-way run at 460,800 baud with no dropped data or checksum errors. J. Nick Koston reviewed the work.

articles.title: Music Assistant puts music sharing controls in view
articles.dek: Administrators gain an access dialog, while personal playlists acquire their own sharing rules.
body: Music Assistant gives household administrators a visible way to choose who owns a music source and who may use it. The source settings show ownership and sharing together, and an Access dialog edits them. This supplies the interface for the private-account controls reported yesterday.

Marcel van der Veldt also extends ownership to playlists created in Music Assistant. New personal playlists start private and can be shared with chosen members, all members or everyone, with a separate choice to allow shared editing. Existing playlists keep their household access; playlists supplied by a music service follow that service’s sharing.

Personal-playlist controls still need their interface, and members’ source-management pages await role permissions. Squeezebox menus and the server’s AI tools continue to list every playlist because those requests carry no user identity. Administrators also get a clear explanation when a member’s music sources must be reassigned before the account can become a guest.
articles.continuity: The interface follows yesterday’s server-side source ownership; personal playlists add another layer of household sharing.

articles.title: Local speech recognition starts without an internet check
articles.dek: Cached models load directly from disk instead of stalling an isolated voice server.
body: A local voice server with its speech model already downloaded should not need the internet to start. OHF Voice’s Wyoming Faster Whisper server tries its cached models first, avoiding a Hugging Face connection that could stall startup and send an isolated container into a restart loop.

Michael Hansen applies the approach across the supported recognition backends. A missing model can still trigger a download; the explicit local-files-only option instead fails immediately when the model is absent. The correction also makes FunASR respect the chosen model directory.

articles.title: Apple Watch gives Assist a button and time to listen
articles.dek: A new watch control joins a recording fix that stops quiet pauses from sending unfinished requests.
body: On watchOS 26 and later, Apple Watch owners gain a Control Center shortcut to Home Assistant’s voice assistant, and Apple Watch Ultra owners can also open it with the Action button. The control opens the assistant configured for the watch.

A companion fix lets the wearer decide when a request is finished. Assist previously stopped recording after three seconds below its silence threshold, sometimes sending an incomplete request even though the screen said to tap to send. Recording instead ends when the wearer taps.

articles.title: Danish departure boards reconnect through Rejseplanen’s new service
articles.dek: The integration replaces the retired interface and moves setup into Home Assistant, with an API key required.
body: Home Assistant’s Rejseplanen integration reconnects Danish public-transport departures through the service’s newer interface. The overhaul replaces a connection to the old service, which the contributor says closed in December 2024.

Setup moves from YAML into Home Assistant’s configuration flow, where selected stops provide sensors for their next departures. An API key from Rejseplanen is required, and the integration requests fresh data every five minutes to respect the service’s limits.
The old sensors’ extra attributes are removed; a proposed action for retrieving richer data is still future work. Jacob Warrer makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the overhaul.

articles.title: Assist understands Italian requests to find and play media
articles.dek: Commands can name a track, artist or other media and choose where it should play.
body: Italian speakers gain Assist phrases for searching a media library and playing the result. Francesco Sappa adds requests for songs, artists, albums, playlists, podcasts and other supported media, with an optional player or room.

The language rules account for Italian articles and connecting words so they do not become part of the search itself. The change works through the existing media-search intent and was reviewed by auanasgheps.
